claimed_purpose.text: PerLTQA is designed to evaluate question answering over personal long-term memory, covering both semantic memory (profiles and social relationships) and episodic memory (events and dialogues).
PerLTQA provides structured access to questions, answers, and memory anchors organized by character and memory type.
Benchmark for memory classification, retrieval, and synthesis of Large Language Models

mechanisms.text: The retriever module supports BM25, DPR, and RocketQAv2 as retrieval backends for fetching relevant memory/context entries from a database given a query.
The dataset is in Chinese and incorporates multiple memory types: world knowledge, profiles, social relationships, events, and dialogues.
Context is preprocessed before retrieval by stripping newlines and removing Chinese user/system turn prefixes ('用户: ' and '系统: ').
The retriever operates on Chinese-language text, as evidenced by the Chinese turn prefixes and jieba tokenizer usage.

ledger.claim: The benchmark structures personal memory into two top-level categories: semantic memory (profiles, social relationships) and episodic memory (events, dialogues).
ledger.quote: Class PerLTMem is a tool class to extract the personal memory including semantic_memory(profiles, social relationships) and episodic memory(events and dialogues).
ledger.label: measured

ledger.claim: QA items are paired with 'memory anchors', implying each question is linked to the specific memory segment(s) it draws upon.
ledger.quote: Class PerLTQA is a tool class used to extract the question, answers and memory ahchors.
ledger.label: measured

ledger.claim: Questions are grouped into four subtypes matching the four memory categories: events, social_relationship, profile, and dialogues.
ledger.quote: extract_event_questions ... extract_social_relationship_questions ... extract_profile_questions ... extract_dialogue_questions
ledger.label: measured

ledger.claim: Social relationship entries contain at minimum a '关系' (relationship type) field, indicating the dataset includes Chinese-language relationship labels.
ledger.quote: relationships.append(v["关系"])
ledger.label: measured

ledger.claim: Individual memory records (events, social relationships, dialogues) are addressable by integer id, implying each character has multiple indexed entries per category.
ledger.quote: def extract_social_relationship_by_id(self,character_name, id) ... def extract_events_by_id(self,character_name, id) ... def extract_dialogues_by_id(self, character_name, id)
ledger.label: measured

ledger.claim: The benchmark covers three named task categories: memory classification, memory retrieval, and memory synthesis/fusion.
ledger.quote: PerLTQA is a new benchmark for memory classification, retrieval, and synthesis of Large Language Models.

ledger.claim: BERT-based classification models outperform LLMs such as ChatGLM3 and ChatGPT on the memory classification task within this benchmark.
ledger.quote: BERT-based classification models significantly outperform LLMs such as ChatGLM3 and ChatGPT in the memory classification task
ledger.label: inferred

ledger.claim: Dataset contains 8,593 QA pairs for 30 characters with memory anchors.
ledger.quote: PerLTQA features two types of memory and a comprehensive benchmark of 8,593 questions for 30 characters
ledger.label: measured

ledger.claim: Memory database contains 141 profiles, 1,339 social relationships, 4,501 events, 3,409 dialogues, 25,256 utterances, and 23,697 memory anchors.
ledger.quote: 141 profiles, 1,339 semantic social relationships, 4,501 events and 3,409 dialogues, and 8,593 memory-related evaluation questions... 23,697 memory anchors
ledger.label: measured

ledger.claim: Memory synthesis is evaluated with gpt-3.5-turbo-based correctness and coherence scoring, plus MAP of memory anchors.
ledger.quote: we measure the correctness and coherence of responses with gpt-3.5-turbo-based evaluation method (Zhong et al., 2023) and use MAP (mean average precision) of memory anchors as shown in Eq.(5) to evaluate memory synthesis ability
ledger.label: measured

ledger.claim: MAP formula for memory synthesis: MAP = (1/N) * sum_i [ EM(q_i, mar_i) / NUM(mar_i) ], where EM counts exact matches between query and memory anchors.
ledger.quote: MAP = 1/N * sum_{i=1}^{N} EM(q_i, mar_i) / NUM(mar_i)... EM represents the tally of exact matches between queries and memory anchors, and NUM(mar_i) is the count of memory anchors per question.
ledger.label: measured

ledger.claim: BERT-base achieves best memory classification: weighted precision 95.96%, recall 95.64%, F1 95.74%, accuracy 95.64% on test set.
ledger.quote: the BERT-base model achieves the highest weighted precision (95.96%), weighted recall (95.64%), weighted F1 score (95.74%), and accuracy (95.64%).
ledger.label: inferred

ledger.claim: BM25 achieves highest Recall@1 (0.705) and Recall@2 (0.847) among retrievers; DPR surpasses BM25 at Recall@5 (0.919) but is much slower.
ledger.quote: BM25: R@1=0.705, R@2=0.847, R@3=0.871, R@5=0.895... DPR: R@5=0.919... the retrieval time cost of DPR is substantially higher than BM25 retrieval.
ledger.label: inferred

ledger.claim: gpt-3.5-turbo achieves highest MAP (0.756) and correctness (0.573) in W-MC+R setting for memory synthesis.
ledger.quote: notable increases in precision (MAP peaking at 0.756) and correctness (correctness reaching up to 0.573)
ledger.label: inferred

ledger.claim: Dataset is entirely synthetic (generated by gpt-3.5-turbo) with human validation and annotation for quality control and memory anchors.
ledger.quote: All the content is fictional. Despite our thorough manual screening, there may still be instances where the common knowledge presented does not align with reality.
ledger.label: measured

ledger.claim: Human annotators: three NLP researchers proficient in Chinese and English, paid $20/hour; annotation took four months (~200 hours per annotator).
ledger.quote: we have employed three researchers in the field of natural language who are proficient in both Chinese and English... Each researcher is paid $20 per hour... The design, annotation, and review of the entire dataset took four months, costing approximately an average of about 200 hours per annotator.
ledger.label: measured

ledger.claim: Memory anchors annotated only for 30 characters due to labor intensity.
ledger.quote: Given the intensive labor involved in manual adjustments, we have annotated memory anchors for a limited set of 30 characters.
ledger.label: measured

ledger.claim: Benchmark claimed to cover abilities: temporal/personal memory recall, semantic memory (profiles, social relationships), episodic memory (events, dialogues), and personalized QA.
ledger.quote: PerLTQA features various QA items... The PerLTQA dataset is designed to capture the essence of semantic and episodic memories.
ledger.label: inferred
